note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 63-wire topology, not printed; the page prints no observable, only that the program 'does absolutely nothing constructive' (printedClass no). Wires as printed, no erratum touches Book V p.46; all 63 lines compared against the PDF p.52 page image, including the two flagged lines 4C/3- and 5H/4-, which are electrically load-bearing (4C/3- returns the C bus 1C/2C/3C/4C to minus; 5H/4- is what lets relay 5 short relay 6's coil). Topology: relays 3-4 and relays 1-2 are two identical toggle stages (nH arm on the shared coil end nF, N.O. nG on +, N.C. nJ to the input node; partner arm on the input node, N.O. to the first relay's E, N.C. to its own E), coils returned through their E lamps to the minus C bus. Relay 5 is fed from D13 alone through its indicator lamp; each pass of the wiper over 13 is one input pulse to stage 3-4 (via 5L/5+, 5K/4H), and stage 3-4 passes a pulse to stage 1-2 through 4L-4N on the pulse that sets relay 3. Relay 6 is a polarity reverser on the motor (6H/+, 6L/-, 6J/6K/D17, 6G/6N/6C/D18) that locks through its own indicator lamp (6C on D18) and is unlocked by relay 5 (5H/4- to 5G/6E); its coil is reached from D1 (relays 3, 1 in), D8 (3 in, 1 out) or D4 (3 out, 2 in). Derived cycle from power-on: up to 13 (relays 1-4 in), up to 1, reverse to 13 (1, 2 in), up to 4, reverse to 13 (3, 4 in), up to 8, reverse to 13 (all out), a full turn to 13, repeat. Assumptions, not printed: D17 + / D18 - turns the dial upward (rotary.md section 4, [likely], Tom ruling 2026-10-13); relay 5 pulls through one indicator lamp during one contact dwell (DC asymptote about 45-46 mA on MV601-REF-A against about 44.5 mA pull-in for relay 5, a thin margin helped by the cold filament); each reversal happens inside the contact that caused it (relay 6 pull-in or release well inside the 16.9 degree pad at 45 rpm). Lamps 2 and 6 (on D-contact groups) and lamp 1 / indicator 1 in the relays-1-2-in state (about 583 milli, at the on/dim boundary) are deliberately not asserted.
